title: Aakar Template Families v1 (Avatars)
description: The catalogue of outcome categories. A family is the form a customer's idea takes: a carrier (Avatar) that fuses the idea with an everyday object, one of the parametric object families, the single raw print family, or a hybrid (Jod): a small printed Chhaap that plugs into a bought-in base item (Buniyaad) through a standard Kadi connector. Seeded from packages/design-tokens/families.json, stored in template_families / shelves / hardware_items / base_items / family_bases, edited in the management portal. Code ids stay snake_case English; brand names (codename, name, tagline) are data.

base_items.description: Bought-in bases (Buniyaad) that hybrid families plug into: a steel headphone stand, a key-hook plate, an E27 lamp base, a magnetic dash mount, an acrylic soap box, or a class of the customer's own bottle or pot (customer_owned). Stored in base_items; stock moves through base_stock_movements.

connector_kind.description: The Kadi standards (docs/research/hybrid-products §1): S ribbed press socket, D dovetail rail, M magnetic register, T thread or lamp collar, C compliant rim clip.

connector_form.description: Kadi-C sub-form: a skirt over a cap, a lip inside an opening, or C-jaws over a rim.

connector_thread.description: Kadi-T standard: a camera-tripod or lamp-nipple thread, or an E27 / E14 shade collar (no thread; the holder's ring clamps the collar).

connector_mode.description: Kadi-M: the Chhaap carries magnets in pockets, or a steel disc that holds to the base's magnet.

tolerance_class.description: How much the base's male feature varies piece to piece: machined ± 0.10 mm, molded ± 0.15, wood ± 0.50; ceramic, glass and steel describe customer-owned rims and caps (a class, range_mm, rather than one size).

connector.description: The Kadi a hybrid family's templates cut into the Chhaap. Always the female feature, printed flat without supports; the base presents the male side, or the bought-in adapter_sku does (a nylon dowel, a PETG rail, a steel disc). Templates publish the modelled connector on their descriptor; this is the family's promise, which the API checks against each listed base's interface.

nominal_mm.description: Kadi-S: the pin Ø (8, 12 or 16). Kadi-D: the rail floor width (12). Kadi-T: the thread major Ø, or the collar hole (e27 40.5, e14 28.9). Kadi-M: the disc or magnet Ø. Kadi-C: the cap OD, opening width or rim thickness the clip is sized for.

fit.description: The as-printed condition the connector is modelled for: press_ribbed (Kadi-S), slide (Kadi-D, Kadi-T), pocket (Kadi-M), snap (Kadi-C).

adapter_sku.description: hardware_items sku of the bought-in male part packed with the piece when the base has none of its own.

base_interface.description: What a base presents to the Chhaap: the same Kadi vocabulary as a family's connector, seen from the male side. The API refuses a design whose family connector and base interface disagree on kind or nominal (incompatible_base).

nominal_mm.description: The pin, rail, thread, disc, cap, opening or rim size the base presents; for a customer-owned class, the middle of range_mm.

range_mm.description: Customer-owned bases only: the size class the Chhaap must grip, e.g. [40, 44] for a bottle cap, [6, 12] for a pot rim.

adapter_sku.description: The bought-in male part that bridges this base and the Chhaap, when the base has no pin or rail of its own.

mount_frame.description: Where the Chhaap's connector seat sits on the base, in the base's own frame (the base stands on z = 0 with its centre on the z axis). The storefront places the printed part's seat at origin_mm, its body along up (the connector axis, from the seat into the printed body: +z for a topper on a stand, -z for a shade hanging from a lamp's holder) and its front along forward.

preview_shape.description: A schematic body the geometry service renders as the base's preview GLB (POST /v1/bases/preview) until a photographed or authored model is uploaded. Dimensions in mm; each shape documents its own keys (pillar_stand: foot_d_mm, foot_h_mm, pillar_d_mm, pillar_h_mm, tube_id_mm, tube_od_mm, tube_h_mm; hook_plate: width_mm, height_mm, thickness_mm, hooks, hook_len_mm; lamp_base: foot_d_mm, foot_h_mm, stem_d_mm, stem_h_mm, holder_d_mm, holder_h_mm; puck_mount: puck_d_mm, puck_h_mm, pad_w_mm, pad_h_mm; box: width_mm, depth_mm, height_mm, wall_mm; bottle: body_d_mm, body_h_mm, cap_d_mm, cap_h_mm; pot: top_d_mm, bottom_d_mm, height_mm, rim_t_mm, rim_h_mm).

pbr.description: A three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial preset (the digital materials' shape).

base_item.description: A bought-in base (Buniyaad). The studio stocks it (stock_qty, reorder_level) and ships it assembled with the printed Chhaap, or it is the customer's own object (customer_owned: a size class, nothing shipped, no base price line).

base_material.description: steel, metal, acrylic, plastic, wood, terracotta, glass.

dimensions_mm.description: Width, depth, height of the base as shipped (or of the typical customer-owned object).

weight_g.description: Shipping weight of the base; 0 for a customer-owned one.

unit_cost_paise.description: What the studio pays; the base price line is retail_price_paise, else this cost with the policy's base_markup_pct.

retail_price_paise.description: A fixed customer price for the base, overriding cost × markup.

lead_days.description: Days to ship when the base is in stock; shown as 'ships in N days'.

stock_qty.description: Opening stock in the seed; movements change it afterwards.

preview_glb_url.description: An authored or photographed model, when one exists; else the preview is generated from preview_shape.

finish_pbr.description: How the viewer draws the base (it is shown muted and locked next to the editable Chhaap).

compliance_notes.description: Safety and legal notes for staff and the product page, e.g. LED ≤ 5 W, cabin heat.

available.description: The staff switch: an unavailable base is never offered, and a hybrid family with no available base is not orderable.

default.description: The base a design takes when the request names none; exactly one per hybrid family.

allowed.description: Digital material ids allowed for this family; null means every available material.

content_slot.description: The Chhaap: what personal content a family accepts and where. A template's features_supported must be a subset of accepts.

anchors.description: Anchor ids the consumer UI offers first.

hero_volume.description: True when the family carries a customer's own 3D form (hero_mesh) in a volume anchor.

id.description: Equals `family` in design specs and template descriptors.

codename.description: Brand name shown to customers, e.g. 'Saathi'. Portal-editable.

name.description: Plain descriptor always shown with the codename, e.g. 'Keychain & bag charm'.

kind.description: carrier = an Avatar that carries the customer's idea; object = a parametric object family (PLAN §7.3); raw = the single 'print as it is' family; hybrid = a Jod, a printed Chhaap that plugs into a bought-in base through a Kadi connector (docs/research/hybrid-products).

tier.description: Roadmap slot from the market research; `available` is the staff switch.

shelf.description: Shop shelf (catalog category) this family sits on.

default_template_id.description: Template used when a request names only the family.

environment.description: Default viewer backdrop before a template is chosen: an environment id from the reference data (experience.v1.json environments; the API checks it against the environments table).

hardware.description: Bought-in parts packed with every piece; a template descriptor's hardware overrides this default.

shape_tolerance.description: any: a plate or plinth absorbs whatever shape the content has; constrained: content must satisfy a rule (attachment region, flat top, shell); strict: the functional body is parametric and content only decorates it.

connector.description: Hybrid families only: the Kadi their templates cut.

bases.description: Hybrid families only: the base items this Chhaap fits, in display order, one of them default. Stored in family_bases.

assembly_minutes.description: Studio time to seat the Chhaap on its base (and bond an adapter), priced by the policy's labour rate unless the family rule names an assembly fee.

pair_family_id.description: The other form of the same idea: for a hybrid, the fully printed family (and the reverse), so the studio can show 'Whole or plug-in?' side by side.

typical_print_minutes.description: Printer time of a typical piece at the default size, for the compare card ('about 3 printer-hours').
